newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Occidental mounts rival Wascana bid.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Occidental mounts rival Wascana bid.

text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. emerged on Tuesday as a white knight for Wascana Energy Inc. with a C$2 billion ($1.5 billion) all-cash bid that tops a cash-and-stock offer from Talisman Energy Inc.

The proposal, which would make Calgary-based CanOxy the third-largest oil and gas exploration and production company in Canada, eclisped a C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion) hostile cash-and-stock offer from Talisman.

Wascana, which had told investors that it was confident a rival bidder would step forward, said its board of directors was recommending shareholders accept the new offer, which is worth C$20.50 ($14.97) a share offer.
Talisman officials could not be reached for comment.

CanOxy, 30 percent-owned by Occidental Petroleum Corp. of Los Angeles, had been touted by analysts as a top contender for Wascana because of its financial strength and its large operations in Saskatchewan. Wascana is based in Regina, Saskatchewan.
"This is one of those unique opportunities where all parties come away from this deal with a win," CanOxy Chief Executive David Hentschel said.
The CanOxy bid represents a 25 percent premium to the closing price of Wascana shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Feb. 11, the day before Talisman announced its bid.
It is also 13 percent higher than the share-swap value of Talisman's offer of C$18.13 ($13.23) a Wascana share at the close on Monday, the companies said.
CanOxy, whose Canadian operations would grow to roughly the same size as its international business with the deal, said it would fund the merger from internal cash flow and debt.
The firms said combined conventional production would total about 115,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in Canada and 264,000 barrels worldwide in 1997.

Under the proposal, Wascana would become a unit of CanOxy and manage the combined conventional oil and gas assets in western Canada. Wascana's head office would stay in Regina, to fit with Saskatchewan government legislation.
Talisman had also said it would keep Wascana's headquarters in Saskatchewan's capital city.
Wascana, known for extensive heavy oil production in the province, is a former government-owned company.
Legislation passed at the end of last year removed a limit for single shareholders owning more than 10 percent of the company's stock. The move opened the door to takeover offers.
The Saskatchewan government still owns 7.3 percent of Wascana stock.
Wascana shares were up C$1.05 to C$20.40 in heavy volume in Toronto after the CanOxy offer. CanOxy climbed C$1.80 to C$25.25 and Talisman rose C35 cents to C$43.95.
